title: Does a state-dependent critic, predicted by theory, rescue learning under alignment shaping?
question: AF found that replacing alignment shaping with approach shaping rescues learning among social peers. tools/theory/shaping_covariance.py gives a general reason: for any stationary shaping potential Phi with lag-1 autocorrelation rho, the shaping reward r = Phi(t+1) - Phi(t) has Cov(Phi(t), r) = -(1 - rho) Var(Phi) <= 0. When presynaptic activity at decision time rises with Phi (food straight ahead drives the sensors hardest and maximises alignment), a covariance learning rule with a scalar reward baseline depresses active synapses on average, whatever the policy. The same derivation predicts a fix that keeps the shaping: a baseline that depends on the state, E[r | state], removes the term (checked numerically on an AR(1) potential: drift -0.30 with a scalar baseline, -0.001 with a state baseline). NeuralMind already has such a critic (critic='state': one reward expectation per binarised sensor state). This study tests the prediction without changing the reward.
background: Same design as AF: fixed dynamics (substeps=32, reset_each_decision, normalize with normalize_to='innate'), no hazards, 1500 training ticks, agent 0 tested frozen on 8 held-out worlds against a fresh untrained agent or group with the same config. Alignment shaping (the default reward) throughout except approach12. critic='state' keys the reward expectation on which of the 11 sensors exceed 0.2. Caveats fixed in advance: the state critic's states are coarse (binarised sensors), so it may remove only part of the bias; and the theory covers the shaping term only, not eating or social rewards. Interpretation rule, fixed in advance: the theory's fix works in NeuralMind if H60a and H60b are supported; it fully rescues social learning if H60c is also supported. No pilot was run. Seeds 3800-3811 and worlds 9940-9947 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Under alignment shaping, a state critic shrinks the learned rise in attacks among social peers
Under alignment shaping, a state critic raises the learning gain among social peers
Under alignment shaping with a state critic, learning pays among social peers
A solo agent still learns under alignment shaping with a state critic
Among social peers, the state critic under alignment shaping differs from approach shaping
